content: The test image shows soybean stems with prominent reddish-brown lesions, particularly around the nodal areas. The stems have clear discoloration extending along their length, with dead plant material above and some green tissue below. Top candidates: **Rhizoctonia**, **Phytophthora**, **Anthracnose**, **Diaporthe**.

**Visual Analysis Summary:**
- Test image: 2-3 soybean stems held by hand showing extensive **reddish-brown lesions** spanning the stem length, particularly prominent at nodal areas
- Upper portions of stems are dead/dried (straw-tan); green tissue visible in background
- Lesions are external surface lesions on stems, reddish-brown in color, near lower/mid stem

**Reference Comparison:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown, sunken, firm lesions at soil line on hypocotyls — color matches well
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown (darker than test image) lesion extending from taproot — less match
- **Anthracnose**: Late-season black fungal bodies on pods/stems — no black specks visible in test
- **Diaporthe**: Gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, black pycnidia in rows — more gray/darker
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Gray/charcoal appearance with microsclerotia — totally different color
- **Tobacco_Streak_Virus**: Pod/leaf symptoms, not stem lesions — no match

The prominent reddish-brown discoloration concentrated at/near nodal areas of stems, with overall reddish-brown hue and dead plant material above, is most consistent with **Rhizoctonia** seedling blight/root rot, which produces characteristic reddish-brown, firm lesions on stems at/near the soil line.
